sources.quote: The 1970s Teddy Boys often sported flamboyant pompadour hairstyles in addition to long sideburns, and they added hairspray to grease/pomade to style their hair.

By 2025 the mod haircut and large sideburns had made a comeback among younger guys in London, Northern England, the Eastern US, and parts of Australia due to a resurgence of interest in 2000s indie rock and 1990s Britpop groups like Oasis.

Facial hair, evolving in its extremity from simply having longer sideburns, to mustaches and goatees, to full-grown beards became popular with young British, European and American men from 1966 onwards.

trends.name: Braids
trends.description: Hair plaited in French, Dutch or fishtail braids.

sources.quote: Another popular hairstyle throughout the decade was the braid, rejuvenated by the likes of Alicia Keys and Lauren Conrad.
Beginning in the late 1990s and continuing into the 2010s, straightened hair and variants of the French braid became popular in Europe.
Dutch braids, twin French braids, side ponytails, and a single chunky side braid were popular styles for those with longer hair throughout the mid and late 2010s.

trends.name: Natural hair
trends.description: Afro-textured hair worn without straightening.

sources.quote: The natural hair movement gained widespread momentum from 2012 to 2016.

Popular styles included curtain bangs, 1980s, 1990s and early 2000s-inspired bangs, hair extensions, ponytails, twin pigtails, French braid, shaggy hair commonly known as the "wolf cut", and natural hair for Black American women.
Textured hair with volume, natural wavy hair, and the bob cut became popular from 2007, even though from the mid-2000s, it continued onwards in both Britain and the USA.

trends.name: Red lipstick
trends.description: Bold red lips.

sources.quote: Women's makeup in the early 1990s primarily consisted of dark red lipstick and neutral eyes.
Red lipstick dominated; Revlon's classic "Cherries in the Snow," introduced in 1953, was among the most fashionable shades.
For evenings and events, the popular look was a smoky eye with long lashes, rosy cheeks and a bold lip.

trends.name: Dark lipstick
trends.description: Lipstick in black, brown, plum or deep wine.

sources.quote: Barbara Stanwyck embodied the look with sharp-shouldered suits, dark lipstick, and lacquered blonde hair.
It became more and more common to see not only black clothes but also stark black eyeliner, hair dyed black, black nail polish, and even black lipstick, on both sexes.

Gothic makeup had broken into the mainstream, having been made up of vamp lipstick (or even black lipstick), heavy mascara and eyeliner, often purple-tinted eye shadow (or else very dark blue), and extremely pale foundation.

trends.name: Pale lipstick
trends.description: Lips painted pale pink or nude.

sources.quote: False eyelashes were in vogue, as was pale lipstick.

Many female mods dressed androgynously, with short haircuts, men's trousers or shirts, flat shoes, and little makeup – often just pale foundation, brown eye shadow, white or pale lipstick and false eyelashes.
The early decade's "erased-mouth" and pale pink lipsticks were replaced by matte red by 2012–13, as sported by celebrities such as Taylor Swift and Rihanna.

trends.name: Lip gloss
trends.description: Shiny, sticky gloss on the lips.

sources.quote: Lip gloss was more popular than lipstick among both women and girls.
This was called "Y2K makeup", consisting of facial glitter and lip gloss.

The style featured slicked-back hair, nude eyeshadow, fluffy brows, dewy skin, bleached eyebrows, liquid blush, and glossy lips, aiming for a casual, effortless appearance that resonated with the relaxed aesthetic favored by Gen Z and Gen Alpha.

trends.name: Bee-stung lips
trends.description: Lips painted small and pouting with a pronounced Cupid's bow.

sources.quote: With the invention of the metal lipstick container as well as compact mirrors, bee-stung lips came into vogue.
Also, with the invention of the swivel lipstick, lipstick was on the rise with bright colors and they applied their lipstick to achieve a cupid's bow and "bee stung" look.
The small rosebud-shaped lips of the 1920s gave way to the 1930s' more natural lip shape, painted in a range of colors that included strong reds as well as lighter, more neutral tints.

trends.name: Pencil-thin eyebrows
trends.description: Eyebrows plucked to a thin arched line.

sources.quote: A defining beauty trend of the era was pencil-thin eyebrows, which were either heavily plucked to form a line or removed altogether and drawn on with pencil.

Foundation and face powder were used for a matte finish; arched brows were drawn with dark eyebrow pencil; eyeliner was applied dramatically on the top lid and often extended outward to widen the eyes.

The style featured slicked-back hair, nude eyeshadow, fluffy brows, dewy skin, bleached eyebrows, liquid blush, and glossy lips, aiming for a casual, effortless appearance that resonated with the relaxed aesthetic favored by Gen Z and Gen Alpha.

trends.name: Smoky eye
trends.description: Dark, smudged eyeliner and shadow around the eyes.

sources.quote: In Britain, the smoky eye look of the late 2000s carried on as a trend in many parts of the country.

trends.name: Winged eyeliner

trends.name: False eyelashes

trends.description: Stretchy synthetic fibre that made clothes skin-tight.

sources.quote: Short, tight Lycra or leather miniskirts and tubular dresses were also worn, as were cropped bolero-style jackets.

trends.name: PVC and vinyl
trends.description: Glossy plastic clothing.

sources.quote: Fashion features much more overt sci-fi influence, with common elements including PVC clothing, futuristic sunglasses, tracksuits, platform shoes, and wearable technology.
Mohair, PVC, and other odd, anachronistic elements of fashion were utilized in outfits.

trends.name: Satin
trends.description: A glossy, fluid fabric.

Typical heavy metal fashions in the UK, US and Australia included faded jeans, leather battle jackets, combat boots, studded belts, black leather jackets like the Schott Perfecto, and iron crosses frequently pilfered from their father's war souvenirs.

trends.name: New Romantics
trends.description: Ruffled shirts, makeup and costume from London's Blitz club.

sources.quote: The New Romantic movement was characterised by flamboyant, eccentric fashion inspired by fashion boutiques such as Kahn and Bell in Birmingham and PX in London.
The origins of the New Romantic fashion and music movement of the early 1980s is often attributed to the Blitz Kids who frequented the club Blitz in London, especially David Bowie.
Early adherents of the movement were often referred to by the press by such names as Blitz Kids, New Dandies and Romantic Rebels.

trends.name: New wave
trends.description: Skinny ties, angular cuts and bright colours after punk.

sources.quote: From the early to mid-1980s, post-punk and new wave music groups influenced mainstream male and female fashion.
The new wave and heavy metal fashion of the 1980s lasted until 1992, when Grunge and hip-hop fashion took over in popularity.
A tamer, less threatening version of the Punk style called "New Wave", which featured jagged hems on clothing and more elaborate embroidery went mainstream in the early 1980s.

trends.name: Goth
trends.description: Black clothes, pale skin and Victorian gloom.

sources.quote: In America, common subcultures of the early 2000s included the nu metal fans and goths who wore black leather duster coats and Tripp pants.
During the mid- to late 1990s, gothic fashion peaked in popularity among American, German and British teenagers seeking to break from the mainstream.
This style, retroactively referred to as Ethergoth, took its inspiration from Siouxsie Sioux and mid-1980s musicians from the 4AD roster like Elizabeth Fraser and Lisa Gerrard.

trends.name: Football casuals
trends.description: Football fans in expensive sportswear labels instead of team colours.

sources.quote: The football casual subculture first appeared in the UK around 1983, when many ex-skinheads began dressing in designer clothing and sportswear to blend into the crowd and avoid police attention at football games.

trends.name: Rave
trends.description: Baggy clothes, smileys and day-glo for dancing all night.

sources.quote: In the rave subculture, fashion trends that had developed in the 1990s persisted.
In the early 1990s the first commercial rave fashion trends developed from this, which were quickly taken up by the fashion industry and marketed under the term clubwear.
In the early 1990s the first commercial rave fashion trends developed from the underground scene, which were quickly taken up by the fashion industry and marketed under the term clubwear.

trends.name: Hip-hop style
trends.description: Sportswear, gold, baggy denim and sneakers from hip-hop culture.

sources.quote: Hip-hop fashion was widely adopted by young people, while indie-inspired styles gained popularity later.

In Europe and North America, hip-hop fashion went mainstream in 1992, with oversized baseball jackets, baggy jeans, bomber jackets, Baja Jackets, and tracksuits popular among young men as casual wear.
According to Chandler and Chandler-Smith (2008), rap and hip-hop were not one specific style, but rather a mix between high-end luxury fashion and what was on the street.

trends.name: Grunge
trends.description: Seattle's flannel, ripped jeans and Doc Martens.

sources.quote: In mid-1992, grunge fashion broke into the mainstream for both sexes.
In 1993, Jacobs as the creative director of women's design at Perry Ellis, debuted a spring collection inspired by grunge.
Overarching trends of the decade included hipster fashion, normcore and minimalist aesthetics, and unisex elements inspired by 1990s grunge.

trends.name: Soft grunge
trends.description: A pastel, Tumblr-era take on 1990s grunge.

sources.quote: Around 2022, the soft grunge fashion style of the early to mid–2010s began to experience a resurgence in popularity due to videos uploaded on TikTok.
Associated with the indie sleaze and emerging soft grunge aesthetic, these designs drew loosely from punk, goth, and 1990s grunge styles but were increasingly detached from subcultural roots.

In the late 2000s, the soft grunge fashion style and Internet aesthetic evolved directly from the indie sleaze trend, once Tumblr users began to merge it with darker fashion elements like fishnets, chokers and combat boots.

trends.name: Kinderwhore
trends.description: Torn babydoll dresses and smeared lipstick, Courtney Love style.

sources.quote: Fairy grunge can be seen as a natural extension of the kinderwhore style — which has deep roots in grunge, but with a more ethereal note.
Cobain's wife, Courtney Love, was mostly known for her "kinderwhore" sense of style used by many female grunge bands.
A very popular look among young women from 1994 to 1995 was the "sexy school girl" look.

trends.name: Britpop
trends.description: Adidas tops, parkas and Union Jacks from mid-1990s British guitar bands.

sources.quote: The period of Britpop's popularity is generally considered to have lasted from 1993 to 1997, with its peak years between 1995 and 1996.

By 2001, popular mainstream trends included tight shirts, bell bottoms, platform shoes, fleeces, cropped tank tops, Union Jack motifs inspired by the Cool Britannia movement, and military inspired clothing, such as flak jackets with camouflage patterns.

Beginning in March 2017, clothing inspired by 1990s Britpop, mod revival and 1970s fashion became popular among young men in the US, UK, Australia, Canada, Ireland, Italy, Hong Kong, and France, especially in beige, cream, sand, orange, blue, brown, dark green, ecru, red, pistachio, and complementary neutral tones.

trends.name: Skater
trends.description: Baggy clothes and Vans from skateboarding.

sources.quote: From 1991 until 1997, flannel shirts became very popular in the US and Australia, due to their use among the skater subculture and grunge bands including Nirvana or Mudhoney.
In the Soviet Union, Australia, East Germany, and America, the skater subculture reached the height of popularity in the mid-'80s.

In the Americas, Britain, Australia, Ethiopia and the Philippines, many skaters wore designer streetwear such as joggers, hoodies, backwards baseball caps, and tracksuits in addition to the typical plaid shirts, ripped jeans and trucker hats.

trends.name: Streetwear
trends.description: Limited-run sneakers, hoodies and logo tees from skate and hip-hop brands, and the collectors who chase them.

sources.quote: Although maximalism gained popularity in high fashion and online communities, streetwear maintained the go-to choice for much of the wider public, especially for those who favor comfort and simplicity.
By the late 1990s, the grunge look became unfashionable, and there was a revival of interest in streetwear clothing, with name brand designers such as Calvin Klein and Ralph Lauren making a comeback.
In the Americas, Malaysia, India, and China, an offshoot of the skater subculture, known as "sneakerheads", dress similarly.

trends.name: Chav
trends.description: British working-class youth in tracksuits, Burberry caps and bling.

sources.quote: Regional styles included the British chav subculture, American gangsta rap fashion and Mexican Cholo fashion.

By the end of the decade, hip-hop fashion had influenced many global subcultures, especially the British chavs with their tracksuits and white trainers, the sneakerheads of America and Asia, and the ICP fans known as Juggalos with their all-black outfits and evil clown corpse paint.

trends.name: Y2K
trends.description: Shiny, futuristic, pink and rhinestoned pop-star style from around the year 2000.

sources.quote: Y2K fashion remained popular from the late 1990s until approximately 2022.
Y2K may also borrow elements from McBling aesthetic, which is sometimes conflated.
Y2K women's fashion from the late 1990s and 2000s became a major influence, especially among social media users.

trends.name: Emo
trends.description: Black skinny jeans, band tees and side fringes.

sources.quote: These included emo, indie, scene, psychobilly, preppy, skater, goth, nu metal, raver culturesrs, as well as hip-hop.

trends.name: Scene
trends.description: Neon emo with backcombed hair and bright extensions.

sources.quote: By early 2009 the most conspicuous subculture in the UK, Australasia and US was the "scene kids."

From 2010 to 2014, the androgynous scene subculture remained common in the West Coast United States, Europe, Australasia, parts of Asia, and South America, especially in the Brazilian city of Fortaleza.
These included emo, indie, scene, psychobilly, preppy, skater, goth, nu metal, raver culturesrs, as well as hip-hop.

trends.name: Hipster
trends.description: Beards, thick glasses, vintage and irony.

sources.quote: These were influenced by the hipster look and its associated lumbersexual trend and campaigns like Movember.
The closely related hipster subculture, which wore vintage clothing ironically rather than as a counterculture statement, emerged in America in the late 2000s to early 2010s.
Characterised by an affordable, messy and lethargic take on vintage fashion styles, especially the 1970s, the style was particularly popular amongst the hipster subculture and indie rock bands.

trends.name: Indie and indie sleaze
trends.description: Guitar-band and party style of skinny jeans, vintage and messy flash photos.

sources.quote: Indie sleaze is a fashion style that was popular in the United States and United Kingdom from approximately 2006 to 2012.
The indie sleaze revival of the 2020s draws inspiration from the American Apparel-aesthetic and the late 2000s indie electronic and electroclash scenes.
Associated with the indie sleaze and emerging soft grunge aesthetic, these designs drew loosely from punk, goth, and 1990s grunge styles but were increasingly detached from subcultural roots.

trends.name: Geek chic
trends.description: Thick glasses and nerdy clothes worn as fashion.

sources.quote: Horn-rimmed glasses were also associated with the geek-chic trend.
American Apparel made normcore a prominent aspect of hipster culture in the US from 2016 onwards.

trends.name: Normcore
trends.description: Deliberately plain, unbranded clothes, Seinfeld style.

sources.quote: American Apparel made normcore a prominent aspect of hipster culture in the US from 2016 onwards.
Normcore is a  unisex fashion trend characterized by unpretentious, average-looking clothing.
Overarching trends of the decade included hipster fashion, normcore and minimalist aesthetics, and unisex elements inspired by 1990s grunge.

trends.name: Vintage and thrift
trends.description: Wearing old and secondhand clothes on purpose.

sources.quote: Common items included mini skirts, bell-bottoms popularized by hippies, vintage clothing from the 1950s and earlier, and the androgynous glam rock and disco styles that introduced platform shoes, bright colors, glitter, and satin.
Vintage and secondhand clothing also became more popular in the Untied Kingdom and the Untied States.
Thrifting also exploded in popularity because of the potential to find valuable pieces of clothing at cheaper prices.

trends.name: Pin-up
trends.description: 1940s and 1950s glamour with victory rolls and red lips.

sources.quote: Later in the decade, it was popular for women to dress like 1950s pin-up girls in polkadot dresses, pencil skirts, sheath dresses, capri pants, platform heels, 1940s style sandals, retro lingerie like garter belts, stockings, babydolls, petticoats, slips, and corsets, and (real or fake) old school tattoos.

trends.name: Western wear
trends.description: Cowboy boots, hats and Western shirts beyond the ranch.

sources.quote: This style, sometimes derisively referred to as drugstore cowboy, urban cowboy or redneck chic, was popular not only in the Southwest, but also in urban areas.
In tandem with the 1970s revival, a second retro trend emerged in the form of blue-collar Americana, particularly in the United States.

From the late 1960s until the early 1970s Western clothing was popular in America due to the success of the spaghetti western and the emergence of a new generation of country musicians like Gram Parsons of the Flying Burrito Brothers, Commander Cody, New Riders of the Purple Sage, and John Denver.

trends.name: Business casual
trends.description: Office dress without a tie.

sources.quote: In the United States, men increasingly wore smart-casual clothing in some professional settings.
In America, an increasing number of men began to dress smart-casual and business casual, a trend kickstarted by Bill Gates of Microsoft.
The business casual look of the 1990s and early 2000s remained common in many parts of the Americas, with jeans, loafers, boat shoes and sneakers being seen as acceptable to wear in the workplace.

trends.name: Cottagecore
trends.description: Floral dresses, puff sleeves and an idealised country life.

sources.quote: Cottagecore was first named on Tumblr in 2018 and is related to similar internet aesthetics including goblincore and dark academia.
An urban cottagecore trend known as "allotment chic" became popular in the UK in the early to mid 2020s, definded by garden workwear.

A nostalgia-driven sub-trend was cottagecore (with subtrends being grandmacore, fairycore, farmcore, and goblincore).The cottagecore style is defined by pastel colors and palettes that evokes a romantic, idealized country aesthetic.

trends.name: Dark academia
trends.description: Tweed, knitwear and old-university gloom.

sources.quote: Cottagecore was first named on Tumblr in 2018 and is related to similar internet aesthetics including goblincore and dark academia.

The dark academia or old money aesthetic of the early to mid 2020s, which combined elements of preppy fashion and gothic fashion, was heavily influenced by 1930s and 1940s fashion, particularly attire worn by students at Oxbridge, Ivy League colleges, and prep schools during the time.

A closely related style, known as "light academia", was characterized by neutral and light colors, including soft blues, pinks, whites, creamy yellows, beige, light greys, light purple, pastel and dusty colors, plaid, stripes, and argyle patterns reminiscent of the preppy look of the early 1980s.

trends.name: Grandpacore
trends.description: Cardigans, loafers and pleated trousers like a cool granddad.

sources.quote: The "grandpacore" fashion trend of 2024, also known as "eclectic grandpa", is characterized by vintage-inspired casual fashion from the late 1940s to early 1960s.

trends.name: Gorpcore
trends.description: Technical hiking gear worn in the city.

sources.quote: Gorpcore is a style that emerged in the late 2010s and early 2020s, coined by Jason Chen in 2017.

trends.name: E-girls and e-boys
trends.description: TikTok-era emo revival with chains, striped tops and painted hearts.

sources.quote: The pop-punk revival of early 2020s saw artists like Machine Gun Kelly and Yungblud influenced by the e-boy look, blending alterative fashion with their music.
In the late 2010s, a softer, goth inspired, style of makeup came into fashion, this was called egirl makeup.
E-kids' fashion is described as being inspired by skater culture, 1990s fashion, anime, hip-hop, kpop, emo rap, and trap metal.

trends.name: Quiet luxury
trends.description: Expensive, logo-free basics for people who don't need to show off.

sources.quote: This trend was also connected to the rise of the “old-money” aesthetic, which was inspired by extravagant European houses and the preference for luxury over displays of wealth or brand association.

Other fashion trends popular from 1997 to 1999 included glamour wear, high-waisted miniskirts, plastic chokers, knee socks associated with the school girl look, tight pants, slip dresses, turtle-neck sweaters, conservative chic, capri pants, high-waisted trousers, and cardigans.
From 2022 to 2025, clothing with bold logos began to lose popularity as fashion trends shifted toward simpler, more minimalist styles.

trends.name: Barbiecore
trends.description: Head-to-toe hot pink.

sources.quote: It became popular in 2022 and 2023, especially following the release of the Barbie movie.

trends.name: Balletcore
trends.description: Wrap tops, leg warmers and ballet flats off the stage.

sources.quote: Ballerina-inspired fashion in the mid-2020s changed both high fashion and street style.

trends.name: Coquette
trends.description: Bows, lace and pink, very girly.

sources.quote: Fairy grunge combined the aesthetics of fairycore, coquette, and grunge.

trends.name: Dopamine dressing
trends.description: Bright, joyful colour to lift the mood.

sources.quote: This "dopamine dressing" movement featured long skirts, belted maxi dresses with thigh splits, and plenty of gold and pearl jewelry, along with neon blue tights.
These chunky pieces echoed 1980s power dressing and 1950s costume jewelry, contributing to the overall look of retro maximalism.
As the decade began, maximalist fashion resurfaced on the runway to express individuality and break away from the previous decades minimalist style.

trends.name: Brat
trends.description: Lime green, messy, party-girl summer of 2024.

sources.quote: Charli XCX also plays a role in the resurgence, with her albums Brat and Brat Summer reflecting this experimental approach to fashion.

Numéro had called the aesthetic the "ancestor" of the Brat style which emerged following the 2024 release of Brat by Charli XCX, as well as citing both the Dare and the Hellp as well as photographer Maya Spangler (also known as Stolenbesos) as contributors to the revival of the aesthetic in 2024.

trends.name: Neo-medieval
trends.description: Chain mail, corsets and tabards inspired by the Middle Ages.

sources.quote: In the winter of 2025, neo-medieval, gothic and folk costume inspired outfits emerged in the US and parts of central Europe as part of a backlash against the increasingly techno-feudal direction taken by modern society.

It has been largely inspired by styles of the late 1970s to late 1980s, the late 1990s to mid-2000s, and elements of Modern Medieval fashion, boho-chic, Indie sleaze and mid-century fashions from the 1940s, 1950s and 1960s.
Sometimes known as bardcore or castle-core, this trend combined feminism with hedonistic luxury fabrics like velvet, lace, jacquard, silk, leather, fur, and brocade.
